description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Consumer Complaint No. 2025-9075281, by Order No. 23130, dated July 29, 2026, denied Gerald Henneghan’s Emergency Motion.
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 
1325 G STREET N.W., SUITE 800 
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20005 

ORDER 

July 29, 2026 

CONSUMER COMPLAINT NO. 2025-9075281, IN THE MATTER OF GERALD 
HENNEGHAN V. POTOMAC ELECTRIC POWER COMPANY, Order No. 23130 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 

1. 
By this Order, the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) denies Gerald Henneghan’s (“Complainant” or “Mr. Henneghan”) Emergency 
Motion.1 

II. 
BACKGROUND 

2. 
In the past two years Mr. Henneghan filed two complaints before the Commission 
against the Potomac Electric Power Company (“Pepco”) In each Complaint, Mr. Henneghan 
asserted the same core claim: that he is not obligated to pay electric bills due to an allegedly 
defective Pepco meter that produces inaccurate readings.2 In response to each Complaint, Pepco 
presented evidence of a Commission referee meter test of Complainant’s meter, indicating that the 
meter was and is operating accurately, and requesting dismissal of the Complaints. The 
Commission issued final orders in each of these proceedings concluding, among other things, that 
Complainant did not meet his burden of proof and failed to present any evidence to substantiate 
his allegations.3 

III. 
DISCUSSION AND DECISION 

3. 
In his current Motion, to which no response was filed by Pepco, Mr. Henneghan

rehashes the same arguments he made in his previous two Complaints, and is seeking the same 
relief he requested in those last two proceedings. Despite Mr. Henneghan’s title for this new 
pleading as an “Emergency Motion,” it is in reality a Petition for Reconsideration of the 
Commission’s final Orders in CC No. 2024-9075272 and CC 2025-9075281, issued on February 
20, 2025, and January 21, 2026, respectively, which is time-barred by D.C. Code § 34-604(b). 
That provision states: “Any public utility or any other person or corporation affected by any final 
order or decision of the Commission may, within 30 days after the publication thereof, file with 
the Commission an application in writing requesting a reconsideration of the matters involved, and 
stating specifically the errors claimed as grounds for such reconsideration.” The Motion, being 
barred by statute, dispenses with any obligation on the part of the Commission to address the 
arguments and assertions therein. 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT: 

4. 
Gerald Henneghan’s Emergency Motion to Restore the Electrical Utility Service to 
His Home and Refund All Payments From 2024 to Date and Void All Billing Statements From 
Pepco From 2024 to Date; to Vacate the Order and the Hearing Officer’s Purported Findings for 
Failing to Conduct an Evidentiary Hearing Consistent with the District of Columbia Court of 
Appeals Decision Vacating Order Nos. 22328 and 22358 and Refund Improperly Implemented 
Rate Increases, is DENIED.
